correctness.rationale: Integrating Lin et al.'s outer-parallel first-variation formula for the chord functional and using their large-radius asymptotic gives the exact deficit identity. Their fixed-perimeter fractional-Willmore inequality makes the integrand nonnegative. Döhrer--Dohmen's prior p=1 fractional-Willmore rigidity identifies equality with disks; the support-function identity for Minkowski addition then transfers disk rigidity from any parallel body back to K. Scaling and the coefficient 2/s in the fractional-perimeter reformulation were checked.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The inspected Lin et al. preprint states disk attainment and uses the same first variation and asymptotic for monotonicity, but does not state the integrated deficit representation or the if-and-only-if equality consequence. Döhrer--Dohmen already prove fractional-Willmore rigidity and that ingredient is excluded from the originality claim. Exact and synonymous searches and the current SCOPE archive did not locate the combined identity or equality result. Recency leaves residual risk of unindexed simultaneous work.

value.rationale: The result converts the monotonicity proof of a newly sharp planar inequality into an exact all-scale deficit formula and closes the equality case in the smooth strictly convex class, exposing fractional-Willmore excess along outer parallel bodies as the precise analytic mechanism behind the deficit.
